channel.title: Chartless guides
channel.description: Free guitar, banjo, mandolin and ukulele chord charts, tuning guides and play-by-ear guides from the maker of Chartless.

item.title: How to tune a mandolin: G D A E, pairs and all — Chartless
item.description: How to tune a mandolin to G D A E: the notes, the 7th-fret method that needs no tuner, getting each pair of strings in unison, and why pairs that are almost matched sound wobbly.

item.title: How to tune a banjo: open G (g D G B D), by ear or with a tuner — Chartless
item.description: How to tune a 5-string banjo to open G (g D G B D): the notes, a fret-by-fret method that needs no tuner, double C tuning, and why the 5th string is the odd one out.

item.title: Mandolin chord chart: 12 chords for G D A E tuning — Chartless
item.description: Mandolin chord chart (G D A E) with diagrams for G, C, D, A, E, F, Bb, Em, Am, Bm, Dm and F#m, plus which chords go together in each key.

item.title: Banjo chord chart: 12 chords in open G tuning — Chartless
item.description: 5-string banjo chord chart in open G (g D G B D) with diagrams for G, C, D, A, E, F, Bb, Em, Am, Bm, Dm and F#m, plus the three chords most bluegrass songs use.

item.title: Guitar chord chart: every major and minor chord — Chartless
item.description: Guitar chord chart for standard tuning: diagrams for all 12 major and 12 minor chords, with the beginner set to learn first.

item.title: Ukulele chord chart: the 12 chords most songs use — Chartless
item.description: Ukulele chord chart (G C E A tuning) with diagrams for C, D, E, F, G, A, Bb, Am, Bm, Dm, Em and F#m, plus the four-chord set that covers most songs.

item.title: What key is this song in? Three ways to find a song's key — Chartless
item.description: How to find what key a song is in: listen for home, check the chords against the key families, or let an app hear it for you. Plus how to tell major from minor.

item.title: Half step down tuning (Eb standard): notes, chords and why bands use it — Chartless
item.description: Half step down tuning (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb): same chord shapes, everything a half step lower. What each shape sounds as, why singers and bands use it, and how to play along when a song is in Eb.

item.title: How to transpose chords to any key (with a chart) — Chartless
item.description: Transpose chords to a new key in two steps: write them as numbers, then read the numbers in the new key. Includes a transposition chart for all 12 keys.

item.title: Open G chords: chart for guitar (D G D G B D) — Chartless
item.description: Open G tuning (D G D G B D) chord chart for guitar: full voicings for C, D, E, F, G, A, Bb, Am, Bm, Dm, Em, F#m.

item.description: DADGAD tuning (D A D G A D) chord chart for guitar: full voicings for C, D, E, F, G, A, Bb, Am, Bm, Dm, Em, F#m.

item.title: Capo chart: what key you're in for every capo fret — Chartless
item.description: Capo chart for guitar: the key you're actually playing in for every capo fret and chord shape, plus the easiest capo and shapes for any key the singer asks for.

item.title: Nashville numbers for worship teams: chart for every key — Chartless
item.description: How to read and write a Nashville number chart, with the 1 through 7 chords for every common worship key. Change the key, keep the chart.

item.title: How to figure out the chords to a song by ear — Chartless
item.description: A five-step method for working out a song's chords by ear: find the key, try the four chords most songs use, follow the bass. Plus what to do when you're stuck.

item.title: Why your guitar sounds out of tune after you tune it — Chartless
item.description: Every string reads dead-on, and the G chord still sounds sour. It's equal temperament, not your ear. Here's why, and the small per-string offsets (in cents) that make open chords ring.
